name: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
problem: Speech has no lexicon and no fixed segmentation, so masked prediction needs a target definition before the loss can be written.
mechanism: Two-stage: pretrain a wav2vec 2.0-style model, then cluster its latent features with k-means offline (100 clusters, two refinement iterations), then train a BERT-style masked prediction of the cluster IDs over masked spans only. The prediction loss on masked regions forces a combined acoustic and language model.
speedup_reported: Matches or beats wav2vec 2.0 on Librispeech (960h) and Libri-light (60,000h) at 10min/1h/10h/100h/960h fine-tune budgets, with the 1B-parameter model improving further. A WER comparison only; the paper states no latency, FLOP or hardware figures, so this record carries no speedup claim.
notes: Venue is IEEE/ACM TASLP vol. 38 issue 1 (Jan 2021) pp. 42-52, confirmed via crossref; the schema's venue enum has no TASLP entry, so 'other' is the honest encoding rather than 'icassp'. HuBERT encoders are shipped in several production ASR stacks as a frozen feature extractor, which is where the inference benefit lands: the encoder runs once per utterance and its output is cached across a beam search.
